# doit_customer_subscription (Resource)

Manages an organization-wide subscription: scheduled email or Slack delivery of a dashboard, a report, a commitment, or any combination of the three, sent to one set of recipients.

Alerts and budgets also appear in the subscriptions API, but they are managed by `doit_alert` and `doit_budget`; importing one of them into this resource fails.

Slack channel IDs are supplied by you; the API has no lookup for them. A channel that is disconnected later stays in `recipients` without an error.

~> **Note:** Creating a subscription requires the Manage Settings permission or the permission for each subscribed type. The first delivery can take up to an hour.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    doit = {
      source  = "doitintl/doit"
      version = "~> 1.0"
    }
  }
}

resource "doit_report" "monthly_costs" {
  name = "Monthly costs"
  config = {
    metrics = [{
      type  = "basic"
      value = "cost"
    }]
    aggregation    = "total"
    time_interval  = "month"
    data_source    = "billing"
    display_values = "actuals_only"
    currency       = "USD"
    layout         = "table"
  }
}

data "doit_commitments" "all" {}

# Email the report every Monday at 08:00 Berlin time, with a PDF and a CSV
# attached, and send the first commitment once a month. All entries share the
# recipients. Both recipient lists are required; use [] for one you do not use.
resource "doit_customer_subscription" "finops" {
  recipients = {
    emails         = ["finops@example.com"]
    slack_channels = []
  }

  subscriptions = [
    {
      type   = "report-subscription"
      source = { id = doit_report.monthly_costs.id }
      schedule = {
        time_zone = "Europe/Berlin"
        # The start day is the calendar date of this instant in time_zone.
        start_date = "2026-11-02T00:00:00+01:00"
        # Only the hour and minute, read in time_zone, are used.
        time      = "2026-11-02T08:00:00+01:00"
        frequency = "Weekly"
      }
      attachments = ["pdf", "csv"]
      pdf_settings = {
        show_filters        = true
        include_table       = true
        include_annotations = false
      }
    },
    {
      type   = "commitment-manager"
      source = { id = data.doit_commitments.all.commitments[0].id }
      schedule = {
        time_zone  = "Europe/Berlin"
        start_date = "2026-11-01T00:00:00+01:00"
        time       = "2026-11-01T09:00:00+01:00"
        frequency  = "Monthly"
      }
    },
  ]
}

# Every two weeks, using a custom frequency.
resource "doit_customer_subscription" "biweekly" {
  recipients = {
    emails         = ["finops@example.com"]
    slack_channels = []
  }

  subscriptions = [{
    type   = "report-subscription"
    source = { id = doit_report.monthly_costs.id }
    schedule = {
      time_zone            = "UTC"
      start_date           = "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z"
      time                 = "2026-11-02T07:00:00Z"
      frequency            = "Custom"
      custom_period_amount = 2
      custom_period_unit   = "Week"
    }
  }]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `recipients` (Attributes) Who receives the deliveries. Both lists are required; use `[]` for an unused list. At least one list must be non-empty. Every entry in `subscriptions` shares these recipients. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--recipients))
- `subscriptions` (Attributes Set) What to deliver: one to three entries, each with a different `type`. Entries that the provider's credentials cannot see are not returned and are left unchanged by updates. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subscriptions))

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_by` (String) Email address of the user or service account that created the subscription.
- `etag` (String) Current ETag of the subscription. The provider sends it with updates and deletes to detect changes made outside Terraform.
- `id` (String) The ID of the subscription.
- `name` (String) Display name, set by the API: the name of the first source (by `type`) followed by `(Dashboard Subscription)`, `(Report Subscription)` or `(Commitment Subscription)`. It follows renames of that source.

<a id="nestedatt--recipients"></a>
### Nested Schema for `recipients`

Required:

- `emails` (List of String) Email addresses that receive the deliveries, in the configured order. Each must be a user or a pending invite in an approved domain of the organization. The API stores them in lowercase; state keeps the configured spelling while the address is unchanged. Use `[]` when email is unused.
- `slack_channels` (List of String) Slack channel IDs (such as `C0123ABCD`), in the configured order. Each must be connected to the organization's Slack workspace. Use `[]` when Slack is unused.


<a id="nestedatt--subscriptions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subscriptions`

Required:

- `schedule` (Attributes) Delivery schedule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subscriptions--schedule))
- `source` (Attributes) The dashboard, report, or commitment to deliver. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subscriptions--source))
- `type` (String) What to deliver: `dashboard-subscription`, `report-subscription`, or `commitment-manager`. Each type may appear once.

Optional:

- `attachments` (List of String) Files to attach to report emails: `pdf`, `csv`, or both, in the configured order. Only `report-subscription` sends files; for other types it must be empty or omitted. When omitted, no files are attached: removing `attachments` from the configuration removes every attachment.
- `pdf_settings` (Attributes) PDF rendering options for report emails. Only allowed for `report-subscription`. When omitted, the API keeps its stored settings (all `true` for a new subscription). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subscriptions--pdf_settings))

Read-Only:

- `permissions` (Attributes) What the provider's credentials may do with this entry. Computed per request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subscriptions--permissions))

<a id="nestedatt--subscriptions--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subscriptions.schedule`

Required:

- `frequency` (String) How often to deliver: `Daily`, `Weekly`, `Monthly`, `Annually`, or `Custom`.
- `start_date` (String) When the schedule starts (RFC 3339). The start day is the calendar date of this instant in `time_zone`, not in UTC: to start on 2026-11-03 in `America/Los_Angeles`, use `2026-11-03T00:00:00-08:00`. The API stores the instant in UTC; state keeps the configured spelling while the instant is unchanged.
- `time` (String) Delivery time (RFC 3339). Only the hour and minute of this instant, read in `time_zone`, are used for deliveries; the date part is stored but has no effect. State keeps the configured spelling while the instant is unchanged.
- `time_zone` (String) IANA time zone used to calculate deliveries, such as `Europe/Berlin`.

Optional:

- `custom_period_amount` (Number) Number of `custom_period_unit` between deliveries (at least 1). Required when `frequency` is `Custom`, and not allowed otherwise.
- `custom_period_unit` (String) Unit for `custom_period_amount`: `Day`, `Week`, `Month`, or `Year`. Required when `frequency` is `Custom`, and not allowed otherwise.

Read-Only:

- `next_at` (String) Next calculated delivery (RFC 3339, UTC).


<a id="nestedatt--subscriptions--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subscriptions.source`

Required:

- `id` (String) ID of the dashboard, report (`doit_report`), or commitment (`doit_commitments`) to deliver.

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) Current name of the source, read from the source itself.


<a id="nestedatt--subscriptions--pdf_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subscriptions.pdf_settings`

Required:

- `include_annotations` (Boolean) Include annotations in the PDF time range.
- `include_table` (Boolean) Include the data table in the PDF.
- `show_filters` (Boolean) Include the summary of the report filters in the PDF.


<a id="nestedatt--subscriptions--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `subscriptions.permissions`

Read-Only:

- `can_delete` (Boolean) Whether the provider's credentials may delete this entry.
- `can_edit_recipients` (Boolean) Whether the provider's credentials may change the recipients.
- `can_unsubscribe` (Boolean) Whether the provider's credentials may remove their own email from the recipients.



<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import using the subscription ID. Alert and budget IDs are rejected; manage
# those with doit_alert and doit_budget.
terraform import doit_customer_subscription.example [subscription_id]
```
